concepts.quote: a local variable has no value until you give it one
concepts.why: States the correct rule that a local variable must be assigned before it holds a readable value, without tracing x in any code.
Correctly relates creation with new to the default values put in every slot, which is why a[0] can be read before assignment.

concepts.quote: a local variable has no value until you give it one
concepts.why: Relates a declaration without initializer to the local staying unassigned until an assignment, though it omits that the read is a compile-time error.

concepts.quote: new fills the array with 0s, but a local variable has no value until you give it one
concepts.why: Correctly contrasts array elements getting defaults at creation with a local variable having no value until assigned, matching the L3 way exactly.
